slot.brief: Ask why H2O2 is stored in dark/waxed bottles with a stabilizer — simple conceptual recall of its decomposition and catalysis.

stem: Why is hydrogen peroxide stored in dark, waxed bottles with a stabilizer?
options: To prevent its oxidation by oxygen in air
To prevent its light-induced decomposition and decomposition catalysed by trace impurities
To increase its rate of decomposition in the dark
To prevent it from dissolving in water

verdicts.working: H₂O₂ decomposes under light, and trace impurities can catalyse its decomposition. Dark bottles and a stabilizer help prevent this.

working:
$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}+\text{O}_2$ 
Light and traces of metal impurities catalyse decomposition.
Dark bottles limit photochemical decomposition; stabilizers suppress impurity-catalysed decomposition.

Independent check: H₂O₂ decomposes under light, and trace impurities can catalyse its decomposition. Dark bottles and a stabilizer help prevent this.
solution:
Hydrogen peroxide decomposes in light and in the presence of trace metal impurities:
$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}+\text{O}_2$$
Dark, waxed bottles limit light-induced decomposition, while a stabilizer suppresses decomposition catalysed by impurities.
